title: Why Do AI Agents Break Rules? How Framing, Context, and Social Signals Shape Compliance
abstract: arXiv:2608.12323v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Specifying a penalty can paradoxically convert a legal obligation into a cost-benefit calculation that favors violation. We demonstrate that this enforcement information paradox systematically occurs in AI agents. While most AI safety evaluations test whether models fail, we investigate why, applying compliance theory from law and economics as a diagnostic tool. We treat compliance theories not as metaphors but as empirical hypotheses and show that each predicts the behavior of a distinct model class. We evaluate our hypotheses across twelve instruction-tuned language models operating as enterprise procurement chatbots. Drawing on theories of deterrence, legitimacy, and expressive law, we show that safety-fine-tuned models maintain compliance broadly, while task-optimized and agentic models treat regulatory signals as mere optimization parameters. translated_title: 为什么AI代理会违反规则？框架、情境和社会信号如何影响合规性
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.12323v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：指定惩罚可能矛盾地将法律义务转化为有利于违规的成本效益计算。我们证明这种执法信息悖论在AI代理中系统性出现。虽然大多数AI安全评估测试模型是否失败，但我们调查原因，应用法律和经济学的合规理论作为诊断工具。我们不将合规理论视为隐喻，而是作为经验假设，并表明每种理论预测不同模型类别的行为。我们在十二个作为企业采购聊天机器人运行的指令调优语言模型中评估我们的假设。借鉴威慑、合法性和表达性法律理论，我们表明安全微调模型广泛保持合规性，而任务优化和代理模型将监管信号视为单纯的优化参数。后一类模型在理论预测的条件下未能合规，例如低执法强度时。
tldr: 本文揭示AI代理中的执法信息悖论，即惩罚设置反而促进违规，并通过合规理论识别出不同模型类别的违规行为模式。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals the enforcement information paradox in AI agents, where specifying penalties paradoxically promotes violation, and uses compliance theory to identify distinct violation patterns across model classes.
